note: Every third-party image the appliance runs, with the tag it is built and tested against. The digest fields are PLACEHOLDERS: Phase 0 (the 60-day Kisaes dogfood baseline) pins every one of them to a real sha256 after the image has run in production for the baseline period. lib/secrets.sh prefers the digest and falls back to the tag while the placeholder 'sha256:TODO-pin-during-phase0' is present, so the appliance is installable today and immutable once Phase 0 lands. Until then, an upstream retag can change what runs on a firm's host without anyone noticing, which is exactly the drift SENT-V-SENT-001 exists to catch.

harness_gating.note: harness_passed records whether the detection/integration harness has been run against THIS tag. upgrade/upgrade.sh REFUSES to move any image with harness_gated:true unless harness_passed is true for the target version. These five families are gated because a silent break in them does not look like an outage: Uptime Kuma's socket.io API is unversioned and changes between releases (Phase 0 note (c)); Vaultwarden migrates its schema on first boot with no supported downgrade and holds the firm's entire credential set; NetBird carries every agent's only path home; Authentik is the IdP for the Sentinel UI; Wazuh IS the detection engine, so a broken decoder set reads as 'quiet' rather than 'down'.

postgres.note: Single shared instance. Databases: sentinel, authentik, vaultwarden, vibe_print (Decision 19).

redis.note: BullMQ queues for sentinel-worker and the Authentik task broker.

authentik.note: One image, two services (server + worker). Serves the Sentinel UI and NetBird only (Decision 21). Authentik release trains rename settings between versions; the harness checks the OIDC apps and group mappings still resolve.

wazuh-manager.note: Manager, indexer, and dashboard must move together — they refuse mixed versions.

wazuh-dashboard.note: Exposed alongside the Sentinel UI with Wazuh RBAC mapped from Sentinel roles.

falco.note: Modern eBPF probe with CAP_BPF/CAP_PERFMON/CAP_SYS_RESOURCE/CAP_SYS_PTRACE, NOT privileged. Privileged fallback only on kernels without BTF, recorded as a risk item. Plan §2.2 requires this image be digest-pinned.

crowdsec.note: LAPI on loopback :8080. Parsers include the Vaultwarden log collection used by the tunnel-mode posture.

cs-firewall-bouncer.note: nftables bouncer on the host. The Cloudflare-side bouncer is a Worker, deployed by modules/edge/cloudflare-worker-bouncer.sh.

netbird-management.note: gRPC through the tunnel with http2Origin=true and an Access BYPASS policy (§2.2). Management/signal/dashboard/relay move together.

netbird-signal.note: gRPC; same tunnel and bypass treatment as management.

netbird-dashboard.note: nb-admin.<domain>, behind Cloudflare Access. Dashboard versioning is independent of the management train.

netbird-relay.note: OPT-IN sub-module, OFF by default. Enabling it opens one UDP port (3478) and is the single approved exception to SENT-E-005 — a logged, QI-approved change (Decision 17).

vaultwarden.note: PostgreSQL backend on the shared instance, separate database (Decision 19). Migrates its schema on first boot with no supported downgrade — an unverified jump is a one-way door for the firm's password vault. Harness must confirm: org policies still apply via the API, ORG_EVENTS_ENABLED still emits, and an unauthenticated /admin request is challenged in tunnel mode.

uptime-kuma.note: v2 line, pinned per Phase 0 note (c). The socket.io API is UNVERSIONED and has changed between releases; the Sentinel monitor adapter is written against this exact build. A break here is silent — monitors simply stop being managed. Phase 0 must confirm the running v2 tag and set harness_passed.

greenbone-gvmd.note: Greenbone Community Edition. scan is DEFAULT OFF. 'stable' is a moving tag upstream — Phase 0 pinning matters more here than anywhere else.

greenbone-ospd-openvas.note: The scanner itself. NET_ADMIN + NET_RAW only, never privileged.

greenbone-pg.note: Greenbone's own Postgres with its pinned extensions — deliberately NOT the shared Sentinel instance, so a feed sync cannot stall the control plane.

greenbone-redis.note: Unix-socket Redis used by the scanner for VT state.

greenbone-mqtt.note: Result bus between ospd-openvas and gvmd.

ntfy.note: Self-hosted push, mesh-bound on 8085 (§2.6). Default notification channel alongside SMTP.

lego.note: sentinel-certs sidecar. ACME DNS-01 through the Cloudflare API for the *.<firm-domain> wildcard, distributed to Vaultwarden, Uptime Kuma, Vibe Print, Authentik, and the Sentinel UI. No private CA anywhere (§2.6).

cloudflared.note: Tunnel connector. Outbound only — the appliance opens no inbound port (§2.2).

restic.note: Built-in backup job, compose profile 'no-vault'. Only enabled for firms that do not run Vibe Vault, so Sentinel is never unbacked (§2.4).

sentinel-api.note: Kisaes-built. Multi-arch amd64/arm64. Runs Drizzle migrations on boot.

sentinel-worker.note: Kisaes-built. Hosts the Uptime Kuma socket.io monitor adapter and the correlation engine.

vibe-printer.note: Kisaes-built, and the SAME image the Vibe Appliance installs (KisaesDevLab/Vibe-Printer) - one packaging of one product across both appliances. REPLACED the vibe-print / vibe-print-release / vibe-print-scanner-inbox trio on 2026-08-28: those three names were never built by any repository, so the print module could not have started. The real product is one container - an API print gateway on :8080 that dials OUT to printers (tcp/9100, tcp/631, or its internal CUPS). It publishes no IPP queues, has no held-release station and no scanner inbox; see modules/print/compose.yml for what that costs Decision 26 and SENT-PR-009. Single-process SQLite by design, so it no longer uses the shared Postgres.
